problem: Public NL/EN switching behaved like a hybrid page/runtime patch instead of one CMS-style shared site-shell responsibility.
root_cause: Header, footer, mega-menu and navigation already shared a canonical shell, but public language switching still mixed static locale routes with browser-driven translation and controls, creating inconsistent same-page switching behavior.
prevention: Public NL/EN controls are owned by the canonical shared site-shell.
Desktop and mobile language controls use real locale links with hreflang.
The localized build binds each switch to the equivalent route in the target language.
Public pages use prebuilt locale routes; runtime translation remains limited to portal or dynamic contexts.
Regression coverage must verify the shared CMS/i18n authority rather than page-specific language patches.
